net.lemnik.eodsql

Class QueryTool

  • java.lang.Object
    • net.lemnik.eodsql.QueryTool

  • public class QueryTool
extends Object

    The QueryTool is used to construct an implementation of a BaseQuery interface. There are two types of BaseQuery that can be constructed with this class:

    1. A simple BaseQuery that locks a Connection to the database (obtained via getQuery(Connection, Class)). This type of query will only allow one connected DataSet at a time, the DataSet.disconnect() method, or the Select.disconnected() flag may be used to get around this limitation. Once a DataSet becomes disconnected, the queries Select methods can be used again. Attempting to call a method when the Connection is in use will result in an IllegalStateException.
    2. A pool-friendly BaseQuery. These can be obtained through the getQuery(DataSource, Class) methods. The reason these queries are pool-friendly is that they do not request a Connection from the DataSource until a method is called, and they release the connections one they are done with it. This also makes them suitable for long-term storage as class-fields instead of local variables.

    The QueryTool also has a notion of a "default" DataSource, which can be set via the setDefaultDataSource(javax.sql.DataSource) method.

    The classes generated by this class are loaded via the Proxy class. The ClassLoader used for the implementation classes is the ContextClassLoader.

    The query classes are validated before any initialization of Proxy's is done, if the query class violates any of the rule's for creating a BaseQuery the creation method will throw an InvalidQueryException

    Author:
    Jason Morris
    See Also:
    BaseQuery, TransactionQuery, Proxy, Thread.getContextClassLoader()

      • setDefaultDataSource

        public static void setDefaultDataSource(DataSource ds)
        Sets the "default" DataSource for the VM. This method must be invoked before getQuery(Class) can be called, the other getQuery methods are unaffected by the default DataSource. This method may not be called with null, and will throw an IllegalArgumentException if the specified DataSource is null.
        Parameters:
        ds - the default DataSource for the VM

      • getQuery

        public static <T extends BaseQuery> T getQuery(Class<T> query)
                                        throws InvalidDataTypeException,
                                               InvalidQueryException

        Returns an instance of a generated implementation for a specific BaseQuery class. After validating that the specified class is a valid query class, this method will return a new implementation of the requested BaseQuery with a reference to the specified DataSource. Each query will keep track of any Connections it opens, and force them closed when it's BaseQuery.close() is called.

        If the default DataSource has not yet been set, this method will throw an IllegalStateException. If the query class violates any of the rule's for a query, this method will result in an IllegalArgumentException.

        Type Parameters:
        T - the implementation type to return
        Parameters:
        query - the BaseQuery to create an implementation of
        Returns:
        an implementation of the specified BaseQuery
        Throws:
        InvalidDataTypeException - if any data-type returned from a method in the query class cannot be mapped
        InvalidQueryException - if any method in the query class is not valid

      • select

        public static <T> DataSet<T> select(Class<T> type,
                                    String query,
                                    Object... parameters)
                             throws InvalidDataTypeException,
                                    InvalidQueryException

        Sometimes you need to perform a less structured "SELECT" than a Query interface allows. Although this method is significantly slower than building a Query interface, it provides needed functionality that a Query interface cannot. The returned DataSet will be connected to the database and will be updateable, and the Connection will be taken from the defaultDataSource.

        This method does no caching of any sort, and the query will be re-parsed each time it is executed. It however provides the same primitive-type abstraction that a Query interface provides you with. The query string is parsed in the same way as a query string passed to an @Select annotation.

        This method is the same as calling select(getDefaultDataSource(), type, query, parameters).

        Type Parameters:
        T - the type to bind each row to
        Parameters:
        type - the data-type you want returned in the DataSet
        query - the SQL query to be executed
        parameters - the parameters to be used in conjunction with the query string.
        Returns:
        a connected DataSet containing the selected rows reflected as the row data-type requested
        Throws:
        InvalidDataTypeException - if the given type cannot be bound as a row data-type
        InvalidQueryException - if the query string given cannot be parsed, or doesn't match the given parameters
        IllegalStateException - is the defaultDataSource has not yet been set
        See Also:
        select(DataSource, Class, String, Object...)

      • update

        public static int update(Connection connection,
                         String query,
                         Object... parameters)
                  throws InvalidDataTypeException,
                         InvalidQueryException

        Sometimes you need to perform a less structured "UPDATE", "INSERT" or "DELETE" than a Query interface allows. Although this method is significantly slower than building a Query interface, it provides needed functionality that a Query interface cannot.

        This method does no caching of any sort, and the query will be re-parsed each time it is executed. It however provides the same primitive-type abstraction that a Query interface provides you with. The query string is parsed in the same way as a query string passed to an @Select annotation.

        Parameters:
        connection - the Connection to use to perform the query
        query - the SQL query to be executed
        parameters - the parameters to be used in conjunction with the query string.
        Returns:
        either (1) the row count for INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statements or (2) 0 for SQL statements that return nothing
        Throws:
        InvalidDataTypeException - if the given type cannot be bound as a row data-type
        InvalidQueryException - if the query string given cannot be parsed, or doesn't match the given parameters
        IllegalArgumentException - is the DataSource provided is null

      • getTypeMap

        public static Map<Class,TypeMapper> getTypeMap()

        Returns the Map that specifies how Java types should be mapped to SQL types and back again. This Map may be modified directly to add new types to the system. The Map may also be used to remove types from the system.

        The TypeMap is not thread-safe for writes. So make sure any writes you wish to do on the TypeMap take place before any database work is done.

        Returns:
        the current data-type Map

      • addQueryFactory

        public static void addQueryFactory(QueryFactory factory)
                            throws IllegalArgumentException

        This method can be used to ensure that a specific type of QueryFactory is known by the QueryTool. If the Java version is 1.6 or higher, the QueryFactory classes should have been discovered on startup by using the ServiceLoader.

        This method is mostly useful if the Java version is 5 (1.5), since the ServiceLoader class will not be available.

        Parameters:
        factory - The factory to ensure is known by the QueryTool
        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if the factory specified is null
        Since:
        2.0

      • removeQueryFactory

        public static void removeQueryFactory(QueryFactory factory)
        The opposite of addQueryFactory(net.lemnik.eodsql.spi.QueryFactory), this method deregisters a specific QueryFactory. This method can be used on any QueryFactory (including those auto-discovered with the ServiceLoader), and will never throw an Exception.
        Parameters:
        factory - the QueryFactory to deregister
        Since:
        2.0

      • addMethodImplementationFactory

        public static void addMethodImplementationFactory(MethodImplementationFactory<? extends Annotation> factory)
                                           throws IllegalArgumentException

        Manually registers a new MethodImplementationFactory object. Under Java 6 there is generally no need to do this, as MethodImplementationFactories are discovered with a ServiceLoader. However under Java 5 you will need to invoke this method with any custom MethodImplementationFactories you have created.

        Note: This method is for advanced use only, and is generally unneeded.

        Parameters:
        factory - the factory to register
        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if the factory is null or does not have a solid (non-wildcard) Annotation type in it's generic-declaration
